get.description:
POST: make a row once, however many times the same request arrives (ADR-0007, 03 §5.10).

The client makes the new row's id and sends it with the row. A phone whose answer was lost sends the
same request again, with the same id, and gets the stored row back, with the same 201: the row as it is
now, so if someone edited it in between, the answer shows the edit. The id names the create: a repeat
gets the stored row whatever else it carries. A route that makes rows builds on this, names what a
create sends (`create_serializer_class`), and writes create_row(), which calls its service.

working_day_over.description: Whether a working day of the month is over: with none, nobody is listed for want of a day.

shop.description: The shop this copy is of: a laptop fills only that shop's database, and writes nothing for another.

min_app_version.description: The lowest app number that may still sync, as on every pull page: an app whose own number is lower fills nothing, and updates first.

cursor.description: The shop's last change number this copy holds: the first pull asks for what came after.

last_device_seq.description: The laptop's own last number: its next record is this plus one, never 1 again.

device_seq.description: Its number on the laptop that made it.

loaded_by.description: The staff member who loaded the rescue file on the sending laptop.

id.description: The period's id, made on the laptop (UUIDv7).

started_at.description: When the laptop's line went, by its clock.

ended_at.description: When it came back, by its clock.

end_unknown.description: True when the laptop's app lost sight of it first: `ended_at` is then the last time it saw it.

in_force.description: The rate in force on the shop's today, or none.

PermissionEnum.description:
* `sale.write` - Write a sale or an order
* `sale.take_payment` - Take a payment
* `sale.hand_over` - Hand the goods over
* `sale.bargain` - Lower a price, down to the floor
* `sale.below_floor_approve` - Approve a price below the floor
* `sale.jumla_switch` - Switch a sale to the jumla price
* `sale.cancel` - Cancel a sale
* `sale.refund` - Refund a sale
* `credit.give` - Sell on credit
* `credit.approve` - Approve credit over a limit
* `debt.view` - See the debts
* `debt.adjust` - Adjust or write off a debt
* `price.change` - Change a price
* `cost.view` - See buying prices and profit
* `product.manage` - Add and change products
* `contact.manage` - Add and change customers, suppliers and partners
* `stock.receive` - Complete a delivery, with its buying prices
* `stock.weigh` - Weigh goods as they arrive
* `stock.loss` - Record a loss
* `stock.count` - Count the stock
* `stock.count_approve` - Approve a stock count
* `stock.transfer` - Move stock from one place to another
* `money.expense` - Pay an expense
* `money.advance` - Give a worker an advance
* `money.withdraw` - Take money out of a drawer
* `drawer.count` - Count a drawer
* `drawer.confirm` - Confirm a counted drawer
* `drawer.approve` - Approve the day
* `staff.manage` - Add workers and give them roles
* `attendance.manage` - Fix attendance
* `pay.run` - Prepare the month's pay
* `pay.approve` - Approve the month's pay
* `settings.manage` - Change the shop's rules and rates
* `device.manage` - Register and block devices
* `flag.review` - Resolve or dismiss a side's flags
* `report.view` - See the reports
* `job.manage` - Run machine jobs
* `production.run` - Record a production run

cursor.description: The last change number this page read, sent or passed over, or the cursor asked when none came: the next pull asks from it.

has_more.description: More changes wait after this page: ask again at once, from its cursor. A page can hold fewer than 1,000 changes and still have more after it.

min_app_version.description: The lowest app number that may still sync: an app whose own number is lower sends what it holds, then updates.

sent_at.description: The laptop's clock as it sends this push.

app_version.description: The app's version on the laptop.

unsent_count.description: How many records the laptop holds unsent, besides these.

first.description:
A duplicate's first answer.

* `accepted` - Accepted
* `invalid` - Invalid

posted_seq.description: The last change number its save took.

code.description: An invalid one's reason, as the error shape names it.

id.description: The document's id, made on the laptop (UUIDv7).

client_time.description: The laptop's clock when it was made: kept, never trusted.

created_by.description: The staff member who made it at the counter.

payload.description: The document itself, in its type's shape.

carried_from.description: Only for a record a rescue file carried here: where it was made.

ReasonEnum.description:
* `outside_job` - Outside the job's days
* `closed_day` - The shop was closed
* `not_working` - Suspended or gone
* `clock_disagrees` - A later tap disagrees
* `time_unknown` - Time not trusted
* `no_in` - No Ingia
* `came_late` - Came late
* `no_out` - No Toka
* `left_early` - Left early

side.description: Empty for a rule of the whole shop.

value.description: The value in force today, as its kind writes it.

TapDoubtEnum.description:
* `not_working` - Suspended or gone
* `clock_disagrees` - A later tap disagrees

yours.description: Whether the month is the viewer's own: then none of its days is theirs to decide (ATT-6).

ready_reasons.description: On the demo, the ready reasons a decision may take, as codes; elsewhere none (ATT-6).

ready_add_reasons.description: On the demo, the ready reasons a tap added may take, as codes; elsewhere none (ATT-13).

ready_void_reasons.description: On the demo, the ready reasons a tap crossed out may take, as codes; elsewhere none (ATT-13).

taps_changed.description: Whether a tap of the day was added, arrived or was crossed out after the day was decided (ATT-13).
